text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Increased 5xx rate on inference-rw-prod (us-east-2a). Metric: inference.errors.5xx spiked from 0.2% -> 4.5% over 3m. Node health: multiple eni detach events detected in us-east-2a. Pager: oncall=james_oncall.

james_oncall: on it. jumping into bridge and will post updates here. please @jin_sre and @oliver_infra for infra triage.

jin_sre: reading logs now — seeing repeated eni detach + 'Network interface detached' around 2024-11-07T15:02Z. a few nodes transitioned to Terminating:Unhealthy in the ASG.

oliver_infra: confirmed from cloudwatch: ENI detach count up ~18 in last 10m for our inference pool in us-east-2a. Route table churn also visible in VPC flow logs.

james_oncall: impact? which endpoints/models impacted? any customer-facing errors?

amy_cs: high-level — we have alerts from 3 customers with elevated latency and some 502/503. most traffic to /v1/generate with model=gpt-infer-1. Customers reported failed requests retrying, some fallbacks to cached responses.

jin_sre: initial mitigation plan: 1) stop new placements in us-east-2a (soft drain) 2) reroute short-lived requests to warm nodes in us-east-2b/cross-region as fallback 3) scale up capacity in us-east-2b.

sean_devops: executing soft drain on us-east-2a ASG now:
```
# reduce desired to current minus new placements
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name rw-infer-us-east-2a --min-size 0 --desired-capacity 0
# cordon out nodes via placement tag
for id in $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:env,Values=prod Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-2a --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' --output text); do
  ./tools/mark-no-new-placements --instance $id
done
```

oliver_infra: enabling traffic steering rule to prefer us-east-2b/c for inference-rw-prod: updated router policy to prefer healthy AZs and added a fallback variant of the model (gpt-infer-1-quant) for lower-memory instances.

james_oncall: turning down concurrency per-instance for the next 15m to prevent cascade. patch applying now.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://zoom.redwood.com/bridge/3723456789 (incident channel: #incident-3723456789). Pager duty: escalation to infra lead.

amy_cs: updating customers: short note sent to top-affected accounts that we see an AZ networking issue and we are routing traffic to healthy AZs. asking for logs if they still see 5xx.

jin_sre: quick diagnostic: looks like ENI detach source is an underlying hypervisor-level NIC reset pattern affecting a subset of instance types. vendor-scoped. opening support case with AWS now (case id: 1234567890).

oliver_infra: AWS case created, they asked for traceroutes and instance ids. collecting and attaching. provider indicated possibility of rate-limited ENI detach due to control-plane throttling in the AZ.

sean_devops: temporary hotfix: added a routing rule to shadow ~10% of traffic to cross-region warm pool (us-west-2) for longer tail requests to keep progress while local warm-ups finish.

james_oncall: monitoring: errors dropped from 4.5% -> 0.8% after reroute but latency increased ~200ms for routed requests. still seeing a handful of failing hosts in us-east-2a.

amy_cs: Customer impact update: 3 customers previously alerted now reporting normal for most calls. one enterprise still sees intermittent 5xx on heavy-batch jobs — recommending retry/backoff.

jin_sre: note for follow-up: need to mark instances from us-east-2a for forced reboot and remove stale ENI attachments once AWS confirms safe window. scheduling maintenance window in 45m.

oliver_infra: created a temporary scaling policy to add 30 nodes in us-east-2b and tagged them as warm-standby for quick routing. also increased kv-cache TTL to reduce backpressure on generation paths.

james_oncall: preparing handoff to night oncall in 40m. if AWS declares AZ healthy we'll do a phased repopulate; otherwise we'll keep traffic steered for the next 6h.

incident-bot: Severity: Sev2. Timeline entry recorded. Attachments: cb/metrics-snapshot-3723456789.png.

sean_devops: saved commands used and logs to /var/incident/3723456789/; runbook updates: added ENI-detach checklist and cross-AZ fallback steps.

amy_cs: posting public status: short message to status.redwood.ai about degraded inference in us-east-2 (partial), routing to healthy AZs, no data loss, ongoing mitigation.

jin_sre: AWS sent preliminary note: 'we see ENI detach spikes possibly due to host-level maintenance; mitigation recommended: avoid scheduling new ENI attachments + scale out to healthy AZs.' They are provisioning host replacements.

james_oncall: summary for handoff: ENI-detach storm in us-east-2a caused capacity evaporation and 5xx spike. mitigations applied: soft drain us-east-2a, traffic steering to us-east-2b/us-west-2, scaled warm pool, reduced per-instance concurrency, AWS case opened. Current state: error rate back near SLO but monitoring for recurrence. handing off to @jin_sre (night) in 30m.

jin_sre: ack — I'll take the next watch. will keep bridge open and post updates. if AWS clears we'll repopulate slowly. otherwise keep steering and coordinate with support.

amy_cs: thanks team. I'll follow up with affected customers and share postmortem notes once incident is stable. :thumbsup:

james_oncall: closing my active pager. moving to watchlist.

incident-bot: Thread closed by james_oncall at 2024-11-07T16:09:59Z (auto-note).
